subject: VPC concurrency cap causing p95 & 5xx — exec alignment requested
message_1_headers:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@meridian.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@meridian.ai
Date: 2027-05-29T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected p95 jumps + 502s after capacity policy change
message_1_body:
Hi Markus,

We started seeing a sustained p95 increase (from ~180ms to ~1.1s) and intermittent 502s across our VPC deployment after the capacity policy change you rolled yesterday evening. The noise began ~02:40 UTC and correlates with higher concurrent decode failures under the new concurrency cap.

We attached a short error slice and a KPI snapshot. This is impacting three production endpoints and blocking a customer demo tomorrow. Can you confirm whether the policy you applied included the concurrency soft-limit you mentioned on the call?

Key observable:
- Concurrent sessions spiked to 420; cap set to 320 at 02:38 UTC.
- KV cache miss rate increased ~12% (we've included short logs).
- Token throughput dropped ~28% on the heavy multisentence requests.

We need an urgent remediation path and an ETA — and if there's any temporary rollback you can do while your team investigates.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of ML Engineering
Meridian Labs

Attachments: meridian_error_slice_20270529.log, kpi_snapshot_20270529.png
message_2_headers:
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@meridian.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-29T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 jumps + 502s after capacity policy change
message_2_body:
Hi Aisha — thanks for the quick flag and the artifacts.

Short answer: we did push a capacity-policy tweak last night intended to throttle noisy sessions for large-batch multisentence decodes. We did set the cluster concurrency soft-cap to 320 for your VPC as a trial. That should have allowed burst above cap briefly, but I can see how strict enforcement might be kicking in.

Immediate plan:
1) Roll the soft-cap back to 480 for your VPC (temporary) — I will trigger this now and monitor for 15 minutes.
2) Run a targeted kernel/quantization probe to reproduce the decode noise in a staging shard.
3) Schedule an exec sync if rollback doesn't clear the 502s — looping in Laura and Priyom to confirm escalation path.

I'll post a rollback confirmation in ~10 minutes. Apologies for the disruption; we should have communicated the trial window more clearly.

— Markus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Note: attaching the SLA usage CSV will help Priyom for the billing/credit discussion.
message_3_headers:
From: ops@meridian.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha@meridian.ai>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@meridian.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:09:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 jumps + 502s after capacity policy change
message_3_body:
Markus — thanks, we saw the partial rollback earlier but 502s persisted on one endpoint (embed-and-rerank) until ~09:30 UTC. We've attached a full slice and a CSV of token billing for the window.

Additional notes from Tom:
> On May 29 09:05 UTC we observe interleaved decode failures with "kv_cache_miss" followed by a rapid reconnect. The pattern suggests the KV cache eviction threshold was hit when concurrency dipped below expected warmup.

This is now affecting downstream batch workers that rely on predictable throughput. We also have a signed demo commitment with an enterprise buyer tomorrow afternoon — if this persists we will need either a hotfix or a fallback model variant enabled for that route.

Tom Brenner
SRE Lead, Meridian Labs

Attachments: SLA-usage-export.csv

Subject: Fwd: Meridian Labs — concurrency cap led to p95/502 spike (need exec coordination)
message_4_body:
Laura / Priyom / Neha — forwarding the Meridian thread. Summary: a policy trial to reduce noisy concurrent decodes set a soft-cap of 320 which has caused increased p95 and intermittent 502s for Meridian's heavy multisentence endpoints. We partially rolled back but residual 502s persisted while the KV cache warmed.

Why I need exec attention:
- Meridian is in an active enterprise negotiation (deal D-6421) and has a paid-demo tomorrow; the impact could jeopardize the milestone and trigger an SLA credit ask.
- The issue exposes a trade-off between the throughput controls we want to push broadly (to reduce cost) and per-customer reliability at scale.

Immediate asks:
- Priyom: assess margin/backstop on committed capacity and advise on short-term credit or reserved burst capacity for Meridian.
- Laura: confirm whether we should temporarily elevate Meridian to a dedicated burst pool (paid) for 48 hours while we investigate kernel evictions.
- Neha: loop in infra SRE for a deep dive into KV cache eviction thresholds and whether warmup behavior changed after the recent runtime optimization.

I will keep Meridian updated. If we need an exec sync, I can be on a 60-minute window from 11:00–14:00 UTC today.

— Markus

Original Meridian thread below.

[Forwarded attachments: meridian_error_slice_20270529.log, kpi_snapshot_20270529.png, SLA-usage-export.csv]

message_5_body:
Hi Aisha / Tom — thanks for the patience and the clear artifacts. We're treating this as a priority.

Immediate decisions: 
1) We will provision a temporary dedicated burst pool for Meridian (48 hours) to stabilize throughput and eliminate the concurrency soft-cap interference. Priyom will follow up with a proposal for credit/compensation tied to the incident.
2) Neha's infra SREs will run a kernel-level replay this afternoon focused on KV cache eviction behavior under rapid concurrency fluctuations; expected initial findings by EOD.
3) Markus' team will validate two mitigations in staging: (a) tuned warmup policy that pins a fraction of KV cache for hot sessions, (b) fallback to a lighter, less-quantized model variant for the embed-and-rerank route.

Status updates: we'll post interim notes to the ticket at https://redwood.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/38420 and share a short executive blurb suitable for Meridian leadership. If Meridian's demo is still at risk, we will move to a 2-hour sync — Markus please confirm your availability.

I will own the exec communication. Priyom, please include the credit calculation and an estimate of incremental cost for the 48-hour burst.

Laura Bennett
